Content:
Let's suppose we only know the values of the functions [MATH: f(x)] and [MATH: g(x)] at [MATH: x=0] along with their derivatives, as given in the table below.

| [MATH: 0] | [MATH: 2] | [MATH: 3] | [MATH: 4] | [MATH: 5] |

Content:
Can we calculate [MATH: \dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x}\Big( f(x)g(x)\Big )] at [MATH: x=0?]

Content:
Using the product rule, we have
[MATH: \dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x}\Big( f(x)g(x)\Big) = f'(x)g(x)+f(x)g'(x).]

Content:
At the point where [MATH: x=0,] this gives
[MATH: \left.\dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x}\Big( f(x)g(x)\Big) \right|_{x=0}	=	f'(0)g(0)+f(0)g'(0).]

Content:
All of these values are given in the table! So, substituting the values from the table into the formula, we conclude that

Content:
[MATH: (d)/(dx)(f(x)g(x))|_{x = 0}|= f^{′}(0)g(0) + f(0)g^{′}(0); = 4 ⋅ 3 + 2 ⋅ 5; = 22.]

sections.normalized_html: For the functions [MATH: f(x)] and [MATH: g(x),] we have [MATH: f(1)=2, \quad f'(1)=2, \quad g(1)=-1, \quad g'(1)=3.] If [MATH: h(x) = \left( f(x)-1 \right)\left(2g(x)+1\right),] compute [MATH: h'(1).]
sections.readable_text:
For the functions [MATH: f(x)] and [MATH: g(x),] we have
[MATH: f(1)=2, \quad f'(1)=2, \quad g(1)=-1, \quad g'(1)=3.]
If [MATH: h(x) = \left( f(x)-1 \right)\left(2g(x)+1\right),] compute [MATH: h'(1).]

sections.normalized_html:
The product rule states that [MATH: \dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x}\Big(uv\Big) = u \dfrac{\textrm d v}{\textrm d x} +v \dfrac{\textrm du}{\textrm d x}.]

Let [MATH: u=f(x)-1] and [MATH: v=2g(x)+1.] Differentiating each, we get [MATH: \dfrac{\textrm d u}{\textrm d x} = f'(x) \qquad \text{and}\qquad \dfrac{\textrm d v}{\textrm d x} = 2g'(x).]

Substituting this into the product rule gives [MATH: h^{′}(x)|= u(dv)/(dx) + v(du)/(dx); = (f(x) − 1) ⋅ 2g^{′}(x) + (2g(x) + 1) ⋅ f^{′}(x); = 2g^{′}(x)(f(x) − 1) + f^{′}(x)(2g(x) + 1).]

At [MATH: x=1], this gives [MATH: h^{′}(1)|= 2g^{′}(1)(f(1) − 1) + f^{′}(1)(2g(1) + 1); = 2 ⋅ 3 ⋅ (2 − 1) + 2 ⋅ (2 ⋅ (− 1) + 1); = 4.]
sections.readable_text:
The product rule states that
[MATH: \dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x}\Big(uv\Big) = u \dfrac{\textrm d v}{\textrm d x} +v \dfrac{\textrm du}{\textrm d x}.]

Let [MATH: u=f(x)-1] and [MATH: v=2g(x)+1.] Differentiating each, we get

Item 1 — Tutorial: Introduction

Content:
Let's suppose we only know the values of the functions [MATH: f(x)] and [MATH: g(x)] at [MATH: x=0] along with their derivatives, as given in the table below.

Content:
| [MATH: x] | [MATH: f(x)] | [MATH: g(x)] | [MATH: f'(x)] | [MATH: g'(x)] |
| [MATH: 0] | [MATH: 2] | [MATH: 3] | [MATH: 4] | [MATH: 5] |

Content:
Can we calculate [MATH: \dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x}\Big( f(x)g(x)\Big )] at [MATH: x=0?]

Content:
Using the product rule, we have
[MATH: \dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x}\Big( f(x)g(x)\Big) = f'(x)g(x)+f(x)g'(x).]

Content:
At the point where [MATH: x=0,] this gives
[MATH: \left.\dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x}\Big( f(x)g(x)\Big) \right|_{x=0}	=	f'(0)g(0)+f(0)g'(0).]

Content:
All of these values are given in the table! So, substituting the values from the table into the formula, we conclude that

Content:
[MATH: (d)/(dx)(f(x)g(x))|_{x = 0}|= f^{′}(0)g(0) + f(0)g^{′}(0); = 4 ⋅ 3 + 2 ⋅ 5; = 22.]

Item 2 — Example: Computing the Derivative of a Product Given the Necessary Data

Example Prompt:

| [MATH: 0] | [MATH: 1] | [MATH: 3] | [MATH: -2] | [MATH: 0] |

Compute [MATH: \dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x}\big(f(x)g(x)\big)] at [MATH: x=0.]

Content:
EXPLANATION

Explanation:
Using the product rule, we get

[MATH: \dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x}\big(f(x)g(x)\big) = f(x)g'(x)+f'(x)g(x).]

At the point where [MATH: x=0], this gives

[MATH: (d)/(dx)(f(x)g(x))|_{x = 0}|= f(0)g^{′}(0) + f^{′}(0)g(0); = 1 ⋅ 0 + 3 ⋅ (− 2); = − 6.]

Compute [MATH: \dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x}\left(\dfrac{h(x)}{z(x)}\right)] at [MATH: x=-1.]

Content:
EXPLANATION

Explanation:
Using the quotient rule, we get
[MATH: \dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x}\left(\dfrac{h(x)}{z(x)}\right) = \dfrac{h'(x)z(x)-h(x)z'(x)}{(z(x))^2}.]

At the point where [MATH: x=-1], this gives
[MATH: (d)/(dx)((h(x))/(z(x)))|_{x = − 1}|= (h^{′}(− 1)z(− 1) − h(− 1)z^{′}(− 1))/((z(− 1))^{2}); = (6 ⋅ 2 − (− 4) ⋅ 3)/(2^{2}); = (24)/(4); = 6.]
